# Background and related work

**Latent planning.** @hanna2026latent define latent planning as internal
representations that (i)~cause a specific future token or concept
(forward planning) and (ii)~shape preceding context to license it
(backward planning). On \(a\)/\(an\) they report that reliable behavioral
success emerges mainly at larger scales. They already use two controls
close to ours. First, they insert the correct or incorrect article and
measure whether the intended noun survives disagreement with the article
(their Fig.~13). Second, in rhyming they feed back intermediate context
generated under steering and then turn steering off (their Fig.~5). We do
not claim to invent token insertion or context replay. We add a complete
six-cell design for an *internal* sparse intervention, full-vocabulary
noun distributions, both article backgrounds, an additive vector split,
dose, and a comparison across selection families. Our local question is
not whether planning exists at scale. It is whether a planning-like
sparse intervention on a small model identifies leftover noun control
after the generated article is held fixed.

**Causal mediation in NLP.** @vig2020mediation formulate total, direct,
and indirect effects for neural NLP and intervene on internal mediators.
@paul2024reasoning treat generated chain-of-thought tokens as mediators of
final answers. The broad claim that generated text can mediate later
outputs is therefore not new. The narrower claim here is that generated
output tokens can mediate the downstream behavioral effect of an
*internal mechanistic intervention*, so matched-token controls are
required before later-token change is read as persistent internal
control. @geiger2025abstraction unifies activation patching, mediation,
causal scrubbing, circuits, sparse features, and steering under causal
abstraction. @chan2022scrubbing test a mechanistic hypothesis by
interventions that should preserve behavior if the hypothesis is
correct. Treated-article insertion with the intervention off is a simple
instance: if the later noun change is carried by the article token,
substituting that token into an unintervened run should recreate most of
the change. @wu2024plan distinguish *pre-caching* (features computed for
future use) from *breadcrumbs* (present-token features that remain useful
later). Our assay does not decide why a representation was computed; it
measures whether an intervention's later effect still exists after the
generated token is controlled.

**Feature circuits and steering.** Attribution graphs over sparse
autoencoders / transcoders estimate contributions among features and
logits [@ameisen2025attribution; @lindsey2025biology;
@dunefsky2024transcoders; @marks2025sparse]. We use `circuit-tracer` with
Gemma Scope 2 cross-layer transcoders [@hanna2025circuittracer;
@gemmascope2] to select features and intervene. Affine skip connections
improve reconstruction but allow MLP computation to bypass sparse
features; we therefore also test a dense residual reference. Graph edges
to future tokens are selection criteria, not already-identified leftover
control; the six cells test that distinction.
